note: Only a pattern, not a document: last year's Q3 print carried a $650m raise and the Boeing deal contemplates a $400m+ offering, while the piloted transition promised for 2026 is still unannounced with seven weeks left - a weak negative into a +12% five-day run-up, shrunk because short interest is 14.9% and rising.

Three guidance legs point one way on documents: no BlueBird has launched since August and the 2026-11-06 8-K reframes external launches as cumulative 2027-2028 against an 'about 45 by early 2027' target, the $150-200m FY revenue guide needs a Q4 a third above the record quarter, and the $1.3bn Blacklift commitment has no capex number yet - all landing on a stock that gapped ~15% into the entry close on an undisclosed-economics JV.

BBVA Peru's quarterly profit fell 28.6% q/q on higher impairments in a filing BAP's US holders rarely read, published after Credicorp last spoke, and Credicorp itself committed to reassess El Nino losses at end-Q3 - yet consensus EPS of $7.51 sits above Q2's $7.29, so a second top-up is not in the bar; shrunk because the stock is already -6.4% in 20 days.

The unchanged FY EBITDA range needs ~$110m in Q4 (~11.5% margin) against 8% in Q2 and a gross margin down 76% to 64% y/y, on the line this name trades on and after two FY EBITDA cuts in 2026; Novo's Wegovy-pill strength and the Lilly deal support revenue, and a 23-27% short with call-bid skew caps the negative.

Subtracting Gasgoo's Jan-Jul table from its Jan-Aug one gives August installs of 126,767 (25.3% share, a 2026 low) and implies September would need ~290-340k to reach the 800-850k Q3 guide - arithmetic no preview has done - corroborated by RoboSense's doubling Q3 ADAS units and Li Auto's weakest October since February, into an unexplained +16% five-day run-up on a name that sold three of its last four prints.

Every fact here is a public 8-K and the baseline already pays for the bear case harder than anything in the evidence - +30.8 vol points of put skew, the day's most extreme - against 63.7% of float short with 8.3 days to cover, so the honest answer is a 20%+ move with no usable sign.

The top line is already pre-released (the 2026-10-13 6-K implies ~$360m against a $358-360m bar) and the stock is +35% in 20 sessions on ASH abstracts, so the call has to justify the run with nothing new on revenue, decelerating CARVYKTI growth and a new outside CEO's first quarter - and both confirmed 2026 prints were sold.

This is the first chance to restate or withdraw the >$1bn 2027 ambition after a settlement forced the company to stop promoting PH-ILD, which was half of YUTREPIA use, into a +74% twenty-day run-up and post-settlement targets raised to $58-70; United Therapeutics' 'moderate near-term switching back' and a 19%-of-shares short with 2.0 days to cover offset much of it.

Up to CHF 53m of tariff refunds sits in reported Q3 gross profit and is excluded from guidance, worth ~CHF 0.13 against a CHF 0.346 EPS bar, so the headline prints large - but LESSONS prices exactly this one-off at a fraction, Deckers had the same refund and still fell 9% on its guide, and the quarter was pre-guided eight days before it ended, so the net is near zero.

Sequential arithmetic off the 13 October pre-release (realised oil, a swing in domestic gas realisations, smaller collar losses) points above the $1.43 consensus and toward the $1.60 whisper, with Diamondback, ConocoPhillips and EOG all beating on the same tape; small because the quarter is pre-released, the Gulf curtailment cuts the Q4 guide and oil beta will dominate the window.

The 'record low' $28m Q3 cash use includes ~$47m of asset-monetisation receipts the pre-release did not split out, so underlying burn is ~$70m+ against $134m of unrestricted cash, and the FY guide needs a Q4 of ~$280m (+44% q/q) that the 15 October release reaffirmed in one line; held small because 21% of shares are short against a 0.08 put/call book and every recent guide reaffirmation was bought.

Management's own August words (both systems ship in Q4 with 'carryover ... into 2027', system revenue recognised over two quarters) plus the 10-Q's 57%-of-$40.7m RPO conversion make the $32.2m Q4 and $42.5m FY bar unreachable, and the FY estimate has not moved since June - so the reset is still to come; no new Q3 system or QCaaS booking was announced either, and a +14% IonQ-sympathy run-up raised the bar.

Tenable, the closest peer, reported after Qualys last spoke with CCB growth accelerating to 9% and a raised outlook, against a billings bar that is only the company's own 'baselined' 7-8% - and CCB is the line that paid +13.8% and +20.6% at the last two upside prints; the October PHP2Shell rally has been fully given back, so no premium is in the price, and the counterweight is a stock trading above every sell-side target.

Everything that could surprise has been pre-released - Neutron's slip to 2027 in the 14 October 8-K, >$1bn of Q3 bookings in the Q2 release, the completed $1.94bn ATM - so what is left is a +27% three-session sector-beta bounce with no company filing behind it, into a name that moved -0.04% on a broad beat last quarter.

AMD - the customer behind ZT Systems and the next-gen program Sanmina pushed into the quarter it guides tonight - guided Oct-Dec to about $17bn, +27% q/q, with Helios deployment increasing substantially, six days ago, and Celestica, Flex and Supermicro all beat and raised on the same months, while the 41% drawdown has no company-level cause anywhere in EDGAR; the offset is real and is why this is not larger: consignment cuts reported ZT revenue, which is exactly what produced -17.5% in July.

The first post-close call has a precedent for raising the synergy number (the predecessor lifted $2bn to $3bn+ in November 2025 and rose 6.4%) and legacy EBITDA has beaten and raised, but the aggregator bar is a pro forma $16.27bn against a legacy quarter of about $7bn, which invites a mechanical 'miss' headline, and the leverage bridge is the thing credit analysts say does not close - so a small positive with a wide band.

A director bought about $12m of stock in the open market on 23 and 26 October - after the quarter closed and with sight of the launch's first five weeks of enrollment data - into a Q3 revenue bar of $0.28-0.30m that is a placeholder a stocking quarter across five specialty pharmacies can clear several times, with 18.2% of shares short at 12.7 days to cover; the +28 put skew argues the other way but sits on a 1,917-contract chain at 55% of mid, which is not a statement.

The fundamental read is positive - Magnite's CTV beat its own guide after TTD's August bar was set, record $11.87bn political spend, and a 15% workforce cut made after the guide was given - but the entry close is struck after +20.8% in five sessions and about +15% intraday on exactly that 'low bar' thesis, above the average target, on a name that fell after seven of its last eight prints including beats.

The stock put in its best week in five months on expectations of 'bumper forecasts' and a pre-order number Zelnick has said on the record the company will not disclose, with the Street's FY27 bookings already above the company's reiterated $8.0-8.2bn and four brokers trimming targets into the print - a reiterate ten days before launch is the most likely release and it does not deliver what the call-rich option book paid for.

The FY EBITDA guide values unsold cargos at $12.50-13.50/MMBtu with $180-210m of EBITDA per dollar while TTF has traded at $27-28, and Cheniere raised its own 2026 guide by about $0.85bn on 29 October after VG last spoke, so a raise is likely into a stock down 10% in 20 days; the 7 October pre-release also gives 465.8 TBtu at a $6.79 fee against Q2's $6.45 on the same volume, which no preview has turned into the ~$2.6bn it implies against a consensus EPS below Q2's.
